newsitem.title: BELGIUM: French lose hold on top EU trade post.
newsitem.headline: French lose hold on top EU trade post.

text.p: France lost a decade-long hold on a key European Union trade post on Thursday with the appointment of Briton Roderick Abbott as the EU's new ambassador to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in Geneva.
A European Commission spokesman said Abbott -- currently head of WTO relations at the Commission -- will replace Jean-Pierre Leng in what is one of the EU's most important trade offices.
Leng, retiring after two years in the job, replaced fellow French national Tran Van Tinh who served almost 10 years in Geneva.
Trade policy is one area where the Commission -- the EU's executive -- operates with fewer fetters than often accompany policy making for the 15-nation bloc.

But France, a sometimes reluctant follower of EU-wide trade policy, has managed to corner the top Geneva job. As a result, analysts say, the French government has managed to "back stop" its interests.
French officials were not immediatley available to comment, but EU sources said there was no dispute over Abbott's appointment, saying it was just reward for his impartial 20-year service.
Abbott's appointment is one of a number of senior changes due at the Commission's trade department.

Horst Krenzler, long-time director-general of the department and effectively the EU's most senior trade civil servant -- is also due to retire soon and speculation is mounting as to who will replace him.
News reports have suggested the job might go to Nikolaus van der Pas, currently the Commission's chief spokesman and formerly a senior trade department official.
Sources say Abbott's current job is to go to Robert Madelin, currently the head of European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan's office.
